notes: The Missouri All-State Choir is administered by the Missouri Choral Directors Association (MCDA), an affiliate of the Missouri Music Educators Association (MMEA); the choir performs at the MMEA Conference at Tan-Tar-A / Margaritaville Lake Resort, Lake Ozark (Osage Beach area), MO. MCDA has published the 2027 event dates (January 27-30, 2027) and the $180 participation fee on its All-State Choir page. However, the linked 'All-District/All-State Procedures Handbook' is still the edition titled 2025-2026 — all requirement, scoring, and fee detail below is drawn from that 2025-2026 handbook and has NOT been re-published for 2026-27. Audition dates are set by each of the individual MMEA districts and were not published on MCDA's site at the time of retrieval.

organization.name: Missouri Choral Directors Association
organization.description: MCDA is the Missouri state chapter of the American Choral Directors Association. It administers the Missouri All-State Choir and the All-District Choirs, publishes the All-District/All-State Procedures Handbook, and runs a summer conference and summer honor choirs.

sources.name: District Choir & Missouri All-State Choir: Information for Parents/Students/Directors (2025-2026)

programs.name: Missouri All-State Choir
programs.description: A statewide auditioned high school choir administered by MCDA. Students first audition for and participate in their MMEA District Choir (solo audition plus a recorded music-literacy audition); students who qualify then take an additional quartet audition for the Missouri All-State Choir. The choir rehearses at pre-MMEA rehearsals and performs at the MMEA Conference.

dates.title: 2027 Missouri All-State Choir
dates.description: Tan-Tar-A Resort at Margaritaville, Lake Ozark, MO. Clinician: Pearl Shangkuan.

requirements.title: MSHSAA eligibility and school certification
requirements.description: District Choir and the Missouri All-State Choir are competitive, MSHSAA-sanctioned events. The student's school must be an MSHSAA member and each school must certify its students' MSHSAA eligibility, including the citizenship by-law (2.2.1) and faculty supervision by-law (1.3.1). From the 2025-2026 handbook.

requirements.title: Grade levels
requirements.description: Per MSHSAA By-Law 2.10.1, All-State membership is drawn from students in 11th and 12th grade at the start of the school year. District Choir membership may also include 9th and 10th graders; the grades eligible for District Choir are set by each individual district. Students who graduate in December are not eligible to participate. From the 2025-2026 handbook.

requirements.title: School ensemble participation
requirements.description: A student auditioning for a District/All-State performing group must be a member of the corresponding high school ensemble at their school. If a school has no high school choir, students from that school may still audition. From the 2025-2026 handbook.

requirements.title: District Choir audition components
requirements.description: Both components must be completed: (1) a solo audition and (2) a music literacy audition. The solo audition is blind, judged by three adjudicators, and runs 60-90 seconds of the selected solo at each district's discretion. Students must bring original (not photocopied) music. From the 2025-2026 handbook.

requirements.title: Music Literacy Audition
requirements.description: The entirety of the Music Literacy Audition is pre-recorded; examples are available on the MCDA website. It includes melodic and part-specific sight-singing, and the student must maintain the tempo given in the recorded audition. From the 2025-2026 handbook.

requirements.title: All-State Quartet Audition
requirements.description: Students who audition for All-State Choir must do so on the same voice part as their District Choir audition. The student is judged blind by three adjudicators. The quartet audition uses a music-minus-one recording in which all voice parts are present except the one auditioning. Students must submit the Audition/Permission Google Form prior to the audition or they will not be permitted to audition. From the 2025-2026 handbook.

requirements.title: Scoring
requirements.description: Standardized scoring rubrics on a 5-point scale are used statewide. The District Choir audition evaluates solo singing and music literacy (melodic sight-singing 10 points, part-specific sight-singing 10 points). The All-State audition evaluates harmonic part-singing within the required choral selection. From the 2025-2026 handbook.

requirements.title: Pre-MMEA rehearsal attendance
requirements.description: All students selected for the Missouri All-State Choir, including alternates, must attend a minimum of 480 minutes (8 hours) of pre-All-State scheduled rehearsals, arriving on time and present for the entirety of each rehearsal. From the 2025-2026 handbook.

requirements.title: Missouri All-State Choir Enrollment Form
requirements.description: Members of and alternates to the Missouri All-State Choir must complete the Enrollment Form within 10 days of notification. It includes the Code of Conduct, Medical Form, and additional MCDA-required information. Students need an official identification document (driver's license, passport, or school ID) and their health insurance information. Honorable Mention designates do not complete this form.

repertoire.title: Exultate Justi
repertoire.notes: MCDA publishes a two-year rotation for the All-State quartet audition selection: 'Fall of even years for All-State in odd years — Exultate Justi (Viadana).' Auditions in fall 2026 for the January 2027 All-State Choir therefore fall on this selection. Score PDF posted on the MCDA ASC Audition Music page.

repertoire.title: O Sing Joyfully
repertoire.notes: The alternate year of the rotation: 'Fall of odd years for All-State in even years.' Score PDF also posted on the MCDA ASC Audition Music page.

fees.description: $180 participation fee per student for members of the Missouri All-State Choir.
Alternates pay a $10 T-shirt fee. Honorable Mention designates pay no fee. From the 2025-2026 handbook.
